description: THE FLAGSHIP OF THE NEW AVIATION HERITAGE CENTRE. Crashed in Madang Province in April 1944 after Captain Charles Davidson and Sergeant John McKenna hit bad weather returning from a mission; both survived a fifteen-day jungle trek; the wreck was subsequently strafed by Japanese fighters. Located by historian Michael Claringbould in 1976 and lifted out by an Australian Defence Force Chinook in October 1984; restored over ten years at RAAF Amberley using parts from about six other A-20s recovered in PNG; sailed from Townsville aboard ADV Reliant on 5 June 2025 and unveiled at the new centre on 8 September 2025. Carries Davidson's pelican emblem. Year_built blank — 42- is a US fiscal order-year prefix; not a build date
aliases: A20; A-20G; Havoc; Boston; Hell'n Pelican II; HellN Pelican II; 42-86786; A20G
museum_name: Papua New Guinea National Museum and Art Gallery
